ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA) of 10 October 1997, SR 951.0; Money Laundering Ordinance (GwV) of 11 November 2015, SR 951.01; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Arts. 305bis, 305ter and 260ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Arts. 620 et seq. and 942 et seq.; Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411); Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities, providing for a non-public central beneficial-ownership register maintained by the Federal Office of Justice and accessible to authorised authorities and obliged financial intermediaries under AMLA Art. 4.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, signatories and ultimate beneficial owners must be screened against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Swiss SECO embargo and sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions where applicable, and OFAC SDN/SSI lists where USD payment rails or US counterparties are involved. PEP status under FATF standards triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth review and senior compliance approval. Screening is mandatory before name clearance, upon onboarding, before each shareholding or financing event, and annually thereafter. Negative findings, unresolved PEP status, or sanctions-list matches constitute disqualifying conditions for incorporation. Records are retained for 10 years under AMLA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index (https://www.zefix.ch) and the electronic portal of the competent cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Swiss Code of Obligations Arts. 942-950, corporate names must be true, clear and non-misleading. The name may be registered in a Swiss official language (German, French, Italian or Romansh), and foreign-language names or non-Latin script must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet and submitted with a sworn or certified translation into an official Swiss language. The name must contain 'AG' or 'SA' and must not mislead as to the registered seat, the legal form or the business scope.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A preliminary name reservation (Voranmeldung) is initially valid for 180 days and may, upon written application before expiry, be extended once for a further 180 days if incorporation is demonstrably in progress. If the commercial register office rejects the requested name, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the competent cantonal supervisory authority within 30 days of the rejection, stating the priority position, the proposed corrected name, and the legal grounds. A further appeal may be brought before the Swiss Federal Administrative Court where required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for active shipyard operation. Use of a virtual office is acceptable only to establish a lawful Swiss registered seat and fiscal correspondence address, but the ISIC 3011 shipyard must prove physical presence through a canton-approved production facility, yard, stores and operative management in Switzerland; a pure virtual or mail-forwarding office alone will not satisfy commercial-substance, industrial-licensing or tax expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximately 65% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first full operating year, with recurring annual risk of 40-60% due to federal and cantonal maritime-safety, environmental, customs, labour and tax-substance inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR; SR 220), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft / societe anonyme), in particular Arts. 625 (minimum capital), 626-628 (articles of association), 629 (paid-up capital at incorporation), 630-631 (deed of incorporation), 643 (registered office), 698 (general meeting powers), and 716b (non-transferable board duties); supplemented by the Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV; SR 221.411).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), supervised by the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenossisches Handelsregisteramt) within the Federal Office of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of incorporation (Errichtungsakt / acte constitutif) executed before a licensed notary public of the Canton of Zug, together with the Articles of Association (Statuten / statuts) and the application for commercial registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung / avis d'inscription).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: CHF 100,000 minimum nominal share capital; at least 20% of each subscribed share, in aggregate not less than CHF 50,000, must be paid up in cash at incorporation. The paid-up capital must be credited to a blocked escrow account at a FINMA-supervised bank in Switzerland and may be released only after entry of the company in the Commercial Register; a bank blocked-account certificate (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) must accompany the registration application.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the incorporation deed and Articles of Association of the Company, dated today, are hereby ratified and adopted; (2) that the subscription of the share capital is accepted and the paid-up capital of CHF 100,000, evidenced by the bank's blocked account confirmation, is approved for release upon registration; (3) that the registered office of the Company is established at Zug, Canton of Zug, Switzerland; (4) that the Board appoints its Chairman, the Chief Executive Officer and the Corporate Secretary with signature rights as prescribed by law; (5) that the officers are authorized to file the registration application with the Commercial Register and to execute all ancillary agreements; (6) that this resolution takes immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Bank Capital Deposit and Blocked-Account Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss depositary bank (cantonal or private bank in Zug); no public government portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the future company's name; remit the minimum paid-in capital of CHF 100,000 (or at least 20% of the nominal capital subject to the CHF 50,000 floor); instruct the bank to issue the blocked-account capital confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) specifying the blocking condition until Commercial Register entry and the authorized payee (future company).
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each founder and officer
Beneficial owner declaration (Form A - wirtschaftlich Berechtigter)
Draft Articles of Association
Source of funds declaration with supporting bank statements
Bank AML/KYC questionnaire and corporate structure description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the transaction, provide enhanced source-of-funds evidence (audited statements, notarized gift or share-purchase agreements); if the account application is rejected, re-apply at an alternative FINMA-supervised bank and resubmit the capital confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Authentication of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary Office of the Canton of Zug (Offentliches Notariat Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders appear personally before the notary, declare the adoption of the Articles of Association and the amount of subscribed and paid-up capital, and execute the deed of incorporation. The notary verifies identity and legal capacity, certifies the deed, and prepares certified extracts and signature declaration for the Commercial Register filing.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all founders
Final Articles of Association (three copies)
Bank blocked-account certificate (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung)
Declaration of compliance with the Lex Koller (acquisition of real estate abroad) if applicable
Personal data and signature specimens of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises objections (sanctions screening, mandate checks, capitalization proof), file supplementary declarations or amended articles the same day; any defect in the deed may be cured by a notarial deed of rectification before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) - electronic eGR portal or paper filing with authenticated signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or the designated officer submits the certified deed of incorporation, Articles of Association, declarations of acceptance of office by board members, and the application requesting registration of the entity, registered office, directors, and signature rules (individual or collective signing authority), together with the blocked-account certificate and domicile consent.
required_dossiers: Certified deed of incorporation
Articles of Association (certified copy)
Signed declarations of acceptance of office by each director and, if not exempt, the external audit firm
Identity documents of directors and authorized signatories
Bank blocked-account certificate
Domicile consent and address confirmation of registered office in Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency letter (Beanstandung), cure the identified formal defects within the stated deadline (typically 10-30 days) by filing a corrective declaration; if registration is denied, appeal to the Cantonal Supervisory Authority for the Commercial Register within 30 days and thereafter to the Federal Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Entry, Legal Personality, and SHAB Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC) and Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the legal examination, the Commercial Register records the company and issues the certified excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug); the company acquires legal personality on the date of entry. The registry causes the incorporation to be published in the SHAB and transmits the mandatory data to the federal statistics service for UID allocation.
required_dossiers: None (registry-initiated); the company must verify the SHAB notice of publication and retain the certified excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication contains errors, file a correction request with the Commercial Register Office within 10 days; third-party objections to the registration are adjudicated under Art. 940 OR by the competent civil court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UID Allocation and Federal Fiscal Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (FSO) for the enterprise identifier (UID); Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for value added tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following registration, the FSO automatically issues the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer). The company then declares its status in the UID portal, obtains VAT registration (if taxable turnover thresholds are expected, including maritime export supplies), and aligns the commercial register data with the federal tax data for customs and foreign trade when importing vessel components.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt
UID data declaration via the UID portal
VAT registration form (if opting for early registration)
Contact and banking details of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If UID or VAT data is inconsistent with the register, submit an amendment request through the UID portal; a negative VAT ruling can be appealed to the ESTV/FTA within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance and Occupational Accident Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Compensation Office of the Canton of Zug (Ausgleichskasse Zug) and Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company and its first employees for OASI/AHV, disability insurance, and loss-of-earnings compensation with the cantonal compensation office; register the shipyard with SUVA for mandatory accident and occupational diseases insurance; open the wage ledger and establish payroll periods before any employee commences work.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt
Employee list with social security numbers
First employment contracts and payroll declaration
SUVA registration form for industrial enterprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, pay social contributions within 60 days to avoid surcharges and apply to the compensation office for remission demonstrating absence of gross negligence; SUVA coverage issues are curable by retroactive notification with good cause.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Economics of the Canton of Zug - Office for Economy and Labor (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit des Kantons Zug), in coordination with the Cantonal Building Inspectorate of Zug and, for maritime technology export controls, the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial enterprise authorization (Bewilligung für industrielle Betriebe / permis d'exploitation pour établissements industriels) under Article 7 of the Swiss Federal Act on Labor in Industry, Crafts and Commerce (Arbeitsgesetz, SR 822.11), supplemented by the cantonal building permit for the shipyard and dry-dock installations (Baubewilligung)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU/OFEV) in coordination with the Cantonal Office for Environmental Protection of Zug (Amt für Umweltschutz Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVPV, SR 814.011) Annex 1 item 33 (shipbuilding installations) where the shipyard works area exceeds 100,000 m² or is located in a sensitive zone; otherwise preliminary screening and registration with the cantonal environmental authority with FOEN notification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: treatment and discharge limits for heavy metals, COD and PAHs under the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV, SR 814.201). Air: VOC, particulate matter and CO2e emissions from painting, blasting and welding lines must comply with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV, SR 814.318.142.1) with abatement efficiency of 85% or more by mass; noise per the Noise Protection Ordinance (LSV, SR 814.41). Waste: hazardous shipyard residues (blasting media, antifouling paints, sludges) shall be tracked under the Waste Movement Ordinance (VEVA, SR 814.610) and consigned exclusively to licensed disposal facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Zug Cantonal Building Insurance (Gebäudeversicherung Zug) covering fire-resistance ratings, escape routes, and flammable-liquid storage; structural static clearance for dry dock, slipway and gantry crane loads by the Cantonal Building Inspectorate (Bauamt Zug); occupational safety audit by SUVA and the cantonal labor inspectorate covering noise, welding fume control, fall protection, and confined-space protocols prior to commissioning; civil defense conformity under cantonal construction law (shelter obligations) where the shipyard includes underground areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA – Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung), VAT and federal income tax divisions, together with the competent cantonal tax administration for cantonal and communal profit taxes; official e-portal: www.estv.admin.ch and the VAT online service 'Mein Konto / Services en ligne'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft in the Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt) and obtain the Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / BUR-ID). Step 2: file federal and cantonal profit-tax registration with the Cantonal Tax Office, including AG statutory capital, seat, and director data, to obtain the corporate tax and direct-tax reference numbers. Step 3: register separately with ESTV for VAT by submitting the standard VAT registration application (Form/Aufnahme der geschäftlichen Tätigkeit; for foreign entities without a Swiss seat, the simplified Swiss VAT registration procedure or the appointment of a fiscal representative under Art. 64 VAT Act), thereby obtaining the Swiss VAT number (format CHE-xxxxx-xxx MWST). Step 4: register with the social security compensation office (AHV/IV/EO/ALV) for payroll and with any maritime-sector licensing authority before constructing or delivering vessels. Step 5: open the Swiss bank accounts and link settlement rails (SWIFT/EBICS and QR-bill) for maritime instalment LCs and escrow accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – the Aktiengesellschaft is taxed as a separate corporate taxpayer at federal, cantonal and communal levels; it has no pass-through status under Swiss tax law. For Swiss VAT the AG is an independently taxable legal person and a taxable person under Art. 10 VAT Act. The worldwide scope of direct taxation applies to a Swiss-resident AG; exports are handled through the indirect tax regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not provide US-style check-the-box or entity-classification elections. Existing elections relevant to a Swiss shipyard AG include: (i) Swiss VAT group taxation ('Unternehmensgruppe') for financially, organisationally and functionally consolidated Swiss entities (Art. 12 para 3 VAT Act); (ii) election between effective input-tax accounting and the simplified flat-rate 'saldo' method (Art. 59 VAT Act); (iii) voluntary VAT registration to recover input VAT, and simplified registration for foreign suppliers of services (Art. 64 VAT Act); (iv) election to pay out Swiss capital contribution reserves (KER/EAC) tax-neutrally to shareholders; (v) optional notional interest deduction-type relief to the extent available under cantonal tax law for financing structures. Hybrid-mismatch elections are not available; stricter Swiss anti-abuse and OECD-aligned hybrid mismatch avoidance rules (HEIV) prevail.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover for Swiss-resident businesses; a foreign shipyard must register for Swiss VAT when its taxable supplies in Switzerland exceed the CHF 100,000 threshold or when it voluntarily opts for registration to claim input VAT recovery. Foreign service suppliers in Switzerland may use the Art. 64 simplified registration procedure if their Swiss receipts are below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or API-based clearing obligation. Mandatory rules instead: (i) every tax invoice must contain the Art. 26 VAT Act details (supplier and recipient VAT numbers, invoice date, description, consideration and applicable VAT rate); (ii) paper and PDF invoices must bear the Swiss QR-bill / QR-payment slip replacing conventional payment slips since 30 June 2020; (iii) B2G invoicing to Swiss federal authorities is executed through PEPPOL-compatible eBill/e-invoicing; (iv) export declarations are filed through the Swiss customs system (NCTS/Landesverwaltung) independently of invoicing; (v) invoices and export substantiation documents must be retained for ten years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT with full input tax credit) applies when the Swiss shipyard delivers a newly built ocean-going container vessel out of Swiss customs territory to a foreign buyer, provided the seller, buyer or a third-party carrier physically transports the goods abroad and economic ownership passes overseas (Art. 23 para 1 let. a VAT Act). Contractual shipbuilding works, outfitting and repair services performed on movable goods for a foreign recipient may also be zero-rated under Art. 23 para 2 let. a/e VAT Act if the recipient is established abroad and the benefit is enjoyed abroad. Delivery to a Swiss-connected buyer, a Swiss port or a customs-free zone without actual export fails zero-rating and triggers the standard 8.1% VAT rate on the full consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Ausfuhrbescheinigung (Swiss Customs NCTS declaration with export date, vessel identification and customs value)
Bill of Lading / Port Delivery Acceptance Certificate proving delivery and discharge at a destination outside Switzerland (original or certified copy)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Currency Credit Advice from a Swiss authorised bank evidencing USD/EUR payment by the overseas buyer within 180 days
Original Commercial Invoice and shipbuilding contract (e.g. Norwegian Sale Form / SHIPSALE) with export terms, Inco determination and vessel ID
Swiss VAT export audit form (MWST export proof) where required by ESTV, plus class survey certificate or proof of newly constructed vessel status.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration and cantonal audit authorities rigorously challenge zero-rating claims lacking coherent customs, transport and payment evidence. Consequences of insufficient or fraudulent export substantiation include: (i) denial of the 0% rate and retrospective reassessment at 8.1% on the full contract price; (ii) arrears interest at 4.5% per annum on the VAT shortfall; (iii) administrative fines of up to three times the evaded tax for intentional tax evasion under VAT Act Arts. 96-97; (iv) criminal prosecution for tax fraud if the vessel export documentation is wilfully falsified; (v) retrospective clawback over the standard five-year limitation period, extended to ten years for deliberate concealment or fraud, exposing all prior export years to reassessment; and (vi) loss of input VAT recovery until restitution is made. Maritime instalment LC or escrow mechanics do not cure documentary insufficiency.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse), operating under the Federal Constitution, the National Bank Act (SR 951.11), and the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (SR 941.10), with anti-money-laundering and banking conduct supervision by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA), sanctions and export-control enforcement by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), and counterparty due-diligence standards imposed through the Swiss Bankers Association Due Diligence Agreement CDB20.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account flows. There is no exchange-control regime, no authorised-dealer intermediation, and no SNB or SECO approval requirement for inbound equity, shareholder loans, trade credits, or outbound profit repatriation by a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. Art. 27 of the Federal Constitution and Art. 3 of the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments guarantee free movement of capital. Dividend and interest distributions by the shipyard AG are subject to Swiss federal withholding tax at 35% (Verrechnungssteuer), fully refundable for Swiss-resident shareholders and substantially relieved under double-taxation treaties for non-resident owners; otherwise, no convertibility restriction, no minimum onshore retention period, and no residency-based limitation applies. For ISIC 3011 vessel construction, invoicing in USD or EUR is unrestricted, proceeds may be held abroad indefinitely, and the SNB operates no minimum exchange-rate target since the 2015 unpegging. Swiss policy rates are in a positive corridor, and there is no penalty or negative interest on non-resident CHF or foreign-currency balances under current SNB policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline on export receipts. A Swiss ocean-container-vessel shipyard may retain USD and EUR proceeds in onshore or offshore accounts indefinitely, apply them to imported steel, engine, and auxiliary-equipment payables, or convert them to CHF at freely negotiated market rates. The only mandatory requirements are documentary: FINMA anti-money-laundering rules and CDB20 oblige the receiving bank to retain origin-of-funds documentation and the underlying shipbuilding contract, and transactions exceeding the enhanced-CDD threshold (normally CHF 50,000 in one or two linked payments) trigger internal record-keeping obligations; no SNB reporting of export earnings is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational Account; Trade Finance and Maritime Instalment Documentary Credits
Operational Account; Export Proceeds Collection Account; Standby LC Counter-Indemnity Account
Operational Account; Rhine and inland-logistics supplier settlement sub-ledger
Operational Account for domestic payroll, VAT, and Swiss social-security payments
Domestic liquidity sub-ledger for transit tolls, fuel cards, and petty cash

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for the mandated payment rails. A Swiss fintech licence under Art. 1b of the Swiss Banking Act or FINMA-recognised payment-institution SRO membership does not permit issuance of commercial documentary credits, maritime instalment LCs, or bank refund guarantees; those require a full category-B Swiss banking licence. Licensed digital-asset banks (Sygnum Bank, SEBA Bank) provide FINMA-graded banking substance and cross-border settlement but do not underwrite vessel-construction trade finance and have low integration with SWIFT-based marine letter-of-credit infrastructure. Unregulated foreign EMI providers (Revolut Business, Airwallex, Wise) cannot hold the construction-milestone escrow balance or issue standby LCs and are restricted by FINMA Circular 2022/14 substance and pass-porting rules. Such EMIs are legally usable only as supplementary FX-settlement wallets for minor supplier payments; core inbound capital escrow, instalment LC collection, and shareholder-loan repayments must run through UBS or ZKB to preserve IFRS audit integrity and CDB20 compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical onboarding for the ISIC 3011 exposure class. Under AMLA (SR 955.0), CDB20, and FINMA Circular 2020/21, at least one director with sole signature and the natural-person beneficial owner must appear in person at the chosen Swiss credit institution. Video-identification is reserved for natural persons opening simple deposit accounts and is not accepted for an AG classified as medium-increased-risk commercial shipbuilding. FINMA expects a structured in-person interview covering the economic purpose of the yard, shipbuilding contract pipeline, customer flag/register, source of advance payments, and ultimate ownership. Non-resident directors may be accepted provided they appear physically at the bank's premises in Switzerland with a certified passport, tax-clearance certificate, and the original articles of association (Statuten). UBS and ZKB permit subsequent remote video onboarding for additional directors after the satisfactory first meeting, but the initial contact is never deferred.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Buyer, shipowner, or charterer registered under an open or low-substance flag state (Panama, Marshall Islands, Liberia, Comoros) with no apparent operational address
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled shipbuilding contract (build specification per ISIC 3011) signed by the OECD-based operating parent; irrevocable instalment documentary credit confirmed by a major European advising bank; CDB20 beneficial-owner declaration with complete passport copies; three years of audited accounts of the buyer; negative SECO, OFAC, and EU sanctions screening; classification-society survey engagement letter (DNV, Lloyd's, Bureau Veritas); explicit confirmation that no flag-state shell sits in the payment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Advance payment or a delivered-stage milestone exceeding 30% of the vessel contract price, or payment routing through a non-OECD clearing corridor before keel-laying evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-issued advance-payment/refund guarantee (URDG 758) payable to the owner; construction-progress certificate by the classification society covering steel-cutting, keel-laying, engine installation, and launching dates; auditor's interim report quantifying burn rates on steel procurement and slipway utilisation; supplier invoices from certified steelworks and engine OEMs; copy of the builder's all-risks and marine construction insurance confirming hull value.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain using Liechtenstein foundations, Marshall Islands LLCs, or discretionary trusts layered above the shipyard AG
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO ladder to natural persons via CDB20 Form A-B with documentary evidence for each intermediate entity; Swiss commercial-register excerpt with board signatures; nominee declarations waiving fiduciary capacity; tax-residence certificates of each UBO and intermediate jurisdiction; negative press and regulatory search results; sworn declaration confirming absence of PEP status or, where applicable, an origin-of-wealth protocol satisfying the bank's PEP policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-adjacent counterparties, grey-fleet vessel bunkering, Russian or isomorphic connections, or dual-use equipment acquisition for the yard
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-to-end real-time sanctions screening of the vessel sale chain, charterparties, and supplier flags against SECO, EU, and OFAC consolidated lists; SECO export-control certificate for the yard's procurement scope; attested dual-use end-use statements for engines, thrusters, and sonar instrumentation; insurance and bunker-licence compliance from the operator; negative Russian-interest attestation and board resolution prohibiting onward transfers; external AML advisory opinion from a Swiss law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on shareholder loans rather than paid-in equity for capitalisation, creating source-of-funds ambiguity and thin-capitalisation suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed shareholders' loan agreement with stated commercial terms, interest rate, and drawdown schedule; bank statements of the lending shareholder proving the wired amounts; tax-clearance certificate from the shareholder's residence jurisdiction; statutory declaration that no Swiss debt-equity ratio threshold is breached; board minutes approving the loan facility; undertaking to provide annual financial statements certified by an auditor licensed under Art. 727a of the Swiss Code of Obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is routed via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or MT202 (cover payment) to the UBS Capital Escrow Account, with ISO 20022 remittance information stating 'EQUI – Capital Increase per Board Resolution DD.MM.YYYY' for share capital or 'LOAN – Shareholder Loan Agreement DD.MM.YYYY' for subordinated debt. For any credit above CHF 50,000, the receiving bank requires: a notarised capital-increase resolution, updated commercial-register excerpt, account purpose statement, CDB20 funds-origin form, and beneficial-owner attestations from the payer's bank. Escrow release is permitted only after confirmation that the capital contribution is recorded in the Swiss Commercial Register and sanctions, PEP, and FATF-recommended monitoring flags are cleared. Cross-border advance instalments under the vessel contract enter by MT103 with purpose 'Export proceeds – vessel construction contract 2024-XX', attract no SNB conversion obligation, and may be maintained in CHF, USD, or EUR per treasury policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for steel slabs, main engines, switchboards, and propeller systems run through (i) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for open-account disbursements against supplier invoices with ISO 20022 remittance data, and (ii) irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued by UBS or ZKB subject to UCP600 and ISBP 821 for major capex procurement. EUR legs clear via TARGET2/EURO1 and USD legs via the issuing Swiss bank's US correspondent network in New-York-dollar wires (CHIPS/Fedwire) under the bank's own liquidity lines. The maritime collection structure uses staged irrevocable instalment LCs (steel-cutting 10%, keel-laying 15%, launching 25%, delivery after sea-trial protocol 50%) under UCP600, paid against classification-society certificates, commercial invoices, drafts, and refund-guarantee certificates; proceeds are swept daily via zero-balance structures into the UBS operational concentration account. Standby LCs under ISP98 secure refund obligations to the buyer for milestone slippage, and SWIFT MT760/MT799 messages provide the documentary backbone for guarantees. No exchange-control or SNB approval is required for any outbound trade payment from Switzerland.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla Deliverable FX Forwards (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, and USD/EUR) under an ISDA 2022 Master Agreement with credit support annex, admissible for forecast vessel-sale proceeds up to 24 months forward without SNB authorisation
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) converting long-dated USD/EUR export receivables into CHF operational liquidity at fixed or floating legs, hedge-accounted as fair-value hedges under IFRS 9
FX Options and zero-premium collars/participating forwards for milestone payments and tender-bid protection, executed only after board treasury-committee approval

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on USD/CHF, technically traded in the interbank market but economically redundant while CHF remains freely convertible and deliverable; reserved for legacy or restricted-capacity corridors
Exchange-traded CHF/USD and CHF/EUR futures cleared via Eurex Clearing for tail hedges and reduction of counterparty credit-risk concentration below ISDA thresholds
FX Swaps (spot-forward rollovers) for short-term working-capital bridging between instalment receipts and disbursement peaks, including USD/EUR swaps avoiding physical conversion
Forward-starting swaps and swaptions in USD/CHF, permitted in-house when the underlying construction-cost payable is evidenced by the documentary LC pipeline

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements, federal and cantonal corporate income tax returns, and adoption of the financial statements at the ordinary annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary general meeting must be held within six months after the balance sheet date; federal and cantonal tax returns are due within the cantonal filing period, generally six to nine months after fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on unpaid tax, administrative late-filing penalties up to CHF 10,000, forced tax assessment by the tax authority, and personal liability of directors for failure to convene the statutory general meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value added tax (VAT) return and settlement of VAT payable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT tax period, ordinarily the calendar year; the exact e-filing deadline is published annually by ESTV
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% per annum, late-filing surcharge up to 3% of tax payable, and administrative fines up to 100% of evaded VAT in cases of willful omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Anticipatory withholding tax declaration and payment on shareholder distributions, dividends, and other taxable profit appropriations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Withholding Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the resolution or due date of the taxable distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, administrative penalties, and joint and several liability of directors and the company for any unremitted anticipatory tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer declaration of salaries and settlement of AHV/IV/EO/ALV social insurance contributions and SUVA accident insurance premiums
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AHV Compensation Fund and Schweizerische Unfallversicherungsanstalt (SUVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the calendar year, or within the extension period granted by the respective compensation fund
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment interest, default contribution penalties up to 10% of unpaid amounts, and criminal fines for false declarations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory ordinary audit is required if the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, or annual average of 250 full-time employees. Companies below these thresholds may elect a restricted audit; companies with fewer than 10 full-time employees may waive the audit entirely only with the unanimous consent of all shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 957 et seq.; Swiss GAAP FER for statutory accounts and consolidated statements; IFRS mandatory for SIX Swiss Exchange-listed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no annual UBO confirmation filing to the commercial register. The board of directors must maintain an up-to-date share register and record transfers as they occur. For bearer shares or bearer-like instruments, holders must disclose their identity and be entered in the share register before exercising voting rights. The general meeting must be supported by a current share register; the auditor, when appointed, verifies consistency of share capital and shareholder entries with the statutory accounts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Officers
Minutes of Board of Directors Meetings
Commercial Register Extract and Articles of Association

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – USD 5,500 per year for a registered office and administrative agent in Zug, Zurich, or Geneva, including mail forwarding and regulatory correspondence handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 18,000 – USD 60,000 per year for a compulsory ordinary audit of a commercial shipbuilding company, depending on turnover, subsidiary consolidation, and group reporting complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate income tax: 8.5% of after-tax profit (equivalent to 7.83% of pre-tax profit); combined federal + cantonal + communal effective rate ranging from approximately 11.9% (Zug) to 21.0% (Vaud) depending on the canton of the registered office; the rate for the Zurich cantonal seat commonly applied to an industrial shipyard is approximately 19.7%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation relief: dividends and capital gains from qualifying participations (≥10% of capital or holding worth ≥ CHF 1 million, held for ≥ 1 year) are exempt from federal, cantonal and communal income tax. Patent box: 90% of qualifying net income from Swiss patented technology and comparable IP rights exempt from federal (from 1 January 2024) and cantonal/communal tax. R&D additional deduction: federal and cantonal schemes allow a supplementary deduction of up to 50% for qualifying R&D expenditure in excess of statutory costs (subject to a maximum of 80-90% of profit dependent on canton). Notional interest deduction on excess equity is available in certain cantons (e.g., Zurich, Geneva). Debt-equity thin capitalisation safe-harbour for manufacturing finance structures; special seagoing-shipping exemptions apply only to ship operators, not shipbuilders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss federal direct tax is assessed on a single integrated cantonal/federal corporate income tax return ('Steuererklärung juristische Personen' / 'Déclaration fiscale personnes morales', e.g., Zurich Form 4 B / Geneva Formula 201), filed with the cantonal tax administration as agent of the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC). Electronic filing is mandatory in all major cantons through the canton-specific secure e-filing portal (e.g., ZH 'Direct federal tax and cantonal tax', GE 'e-Déclaration', VD 'e-Déc' plus the SIDOS system); the federal share is computed and transmitted to the ESTV automatically.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within the period set by the cantonal authority, ordinarily by 31 March of the year following the tax period (Art. 124 para. 1 Federal Act on Direct Tax, DBG); an automatic or granted extension is available on written request up to 30 September (Zurich) or 31 October (Geneva) for corporations with audited accounts, and in any event before the tax period is assessed by a final decision.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit/loss (annual income statement) including the profit before tax of the shipyard, cost of materials, maritime construction financing costs, and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shipyard AGs with permanent establishment in Switzerland report only the PE-imputed profit determined by an OECD-compliant profit split; the global commercial accounts are attached in the annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recharges of non-deductible expenses: hidden profit distributions, excessive interest expense, related-party management fees, depreciation recapture, and 50% of board compensation if conventional remuneration rules are exceeded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign head-office recharges to the Swiss PE must be evidenced by a written cost contribution agreement; the adjusting entries must be disclosed separately to the assessor.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilisation (7-year limit), participation relief (Schachtelabzug), patent box deduction, R&D additional deduction, notional interest deduction (where applicable) and the federal/cantonal part of the tax itself.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Participation relief in the non-resident context applies only if the foreign shareholder's participation is Switzerland-sourced of a Swiss subsidiary; the foreign parent must declare the segment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D (Taxable capital base for cantonal capital tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal/communal capital tax declaration on adjusted taxable equity (gesetzliches Eigenkapital minus participating interests and IP capital, plus hidden reserves), at cantonal rate of approx. 0.01%-0.2%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs are assessed only on the part of the Swiss book equity attributable to the PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 174 DBG (per responsible organ), plus forced assessment by discretionary estimate with a security surcharge on assessed tax; default interest 5% p.a.; late payment interest at federal/cantonal rates; tax evasion (Art. 175/176 DBG) for intentional under-reporting: fine equal to the amount of tax evaded, increased up to 3× in grave cases; tax deception (Art. 186 DBG): imprisonment up to 2 years or fine, in addition to the tax and interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividend distributions of an Aktiengesellschaft, payable by the AG to the Federal Tax Administration, charged to the shareholder-beneficiary subject to refund/treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The foreign parent may invoke the applicable double taxation agreement (DTA) through either: (i) prior 'relief at source' (Entlastungsverfahren an der Quelle) — qualifying parent holding ≥10% of the voting shares continuously for one year and resident in a treaty state obtains a reduction to 0% (or applicable treaty rate) before dividend payment by filing with the paying bank the ESTV relief-at-source declaration (Form 823/823a variants) together with a certified Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) of the current year and the beneficial ownership statement; or (ii) refund procedure (Rückerstattungsverfahren) — the foreign recipient pays 35%, then files the ESTV refund application form (Form R-Us for legal persons) within three years of the taxable event, attaching the TRC issued by the residence state, the board resolution on dividend distribution, and proof of participation holding and custody; the Federal Tax Administration verifies that the candidate is the beneficial owner, meets the DTA limitation-of-benefits clause and the Swiss anti-abuse (treaty shopping) provisions. Dividends to EU-domiciled parent companies with qualifying holdings are reduced to 0% under the EU-Swiss arbitrary equivalent measure framework (reimbursement of the difference between 35% and 0%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss federal withholding tax applies to royalties at 0% (no withholding tax on licence fees; licence income is taxed in the source country of the residence of the beneficial owner; DTA rates with important jurisdictions are 0%, older treaties up to 5%); interest: statutory 35% on interest on Swiss public bond issues and money market instruments payable to non-residents; standard inter-company commercial loans, maritime construction finance and bank debt are not subject to Swiss WHT unless structured as publicly issued obligations; treaty interest rates are 0% under the 2010-policy DTAs (including US-CH), 10% on obsolete portfolio guarantees; interest paid to non-resident lenders from an accrual-based financing of a Swiss shipyard therefore incurs no Swiss source tax when the loan is drafted as a private loan agreement and not as negotiable securities.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland does not codify OECD Local File/Master File thresholds in domestic statute; the ESTV Transfer Pricing Circular (Verrechnungspreis-Rundschreiben, November 2020) applies the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and the documentation duty arises as soon as cross-border related-party transactions are declared in the tax return; in administrative practice contemporaneous TP documentation is expected whenever the aggregate value of controlled transactions exceeds CHF 1 million per counterparty or the AG belongs to a group; Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory for Swiss-headquartered (and secondary/ surrogate) groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CHF 900 million (OECD BEPS threshold), filed electronically with the ESTV within 12 months of the fiscal year-end and exchanged under the multilateral competent authority agreement.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Swiss annex: exit clauses for combined application of methods and the five comparability factors of OECD Ch. I
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has not enacted Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) legislation in the Caribbean/Emirati sense; substance is protected through: (i) corporate residence determined by statutory seat or place of effective management (Art. 50 DBG); (ii) the statutory general anti-abuse rule (Steuerumgehung, Art. 219 DBG) by which structures lacking economic purpose, erected solely to save taxes, are recharacterised — for a shipyard this means that any holding or invoicing entity without personnel, shipyard capacity or decision-making in Switzerland is disregarded; (iii) the anti-hybrid and Limitation of Benefits clauses embedded in DTA relief, and (iv) the Pillar Two Minimum Tax Act (Mindeststeuergesetz, in force 1 January 2024): Swiss-resident groups with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750 million are subject to a 15% qualified global minimum tax through IIR/UTPR and a Swiss qualified domestic top-up tax (QDMTT); the shipyard must model the GloBE effective rate and file the GloBE information return.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Steuerhinterziehung) / Federal and Cantonal Direct Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing shipbuilding profit, overstating raw-material or subcontractor costs, issuing inflated invoices from related suppliers, omitting the 7-year loss carryforward computations, or failing to disclose foreign PE or subsidiary income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to the amount of tax evaded (Art. 175 DBG); in particularly serious cases up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 176 DBG), plus default/evasion interest on the reassessed tax, and exclusion of the deductibility of the fine. Cantonal law attaches parallel penalties up to similar multiples.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The CEO/CFO and the director responsible for accounting are jointly targeted as the acting organ: criminal fines are imposed personally, the share register does not protect the signatory, and the Federal Criminal Court may order a professional ban (Berufsverbot) of up to five years and seizure of assets; civil piercing of the veil (Durchgriffshaftung) applies where the AG is used as a mere facade for the shareholder's personal affairs (e.g., BGE 138 III 195).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Deception (Steuerbetrug) and Withholding Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing falsified audited accounts, forged construction contracts, fictitious charterer invoices or counterfeit tax documents to obtain a dividend refund or treaty relief; failing to withhold and remit 35% Swiss withholding tax on distributed dividends or bond interest; failing to file the monthly/quarterly remittance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to two years or fine (Art. 186 DBG); withholding tax evasion: fine of up to five times the withheld tax under Art. 72 of the Federal Withholding Tax Act and liability for the tax at 100% plus 5% per annum interest; in international group cases the evasion may qualify as criminal money laundering under Art. 305bis SCC with imprisonment up to three years (five years in aggravated cases), confiscation of the proceeds and freezable assets in multiple jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally criminally liable for false certification of the annual accounts and for the failure to deduct the withholding tax (Civil and criminal liability in solidum: the unpaid tax, penalty and interest can be recovered from the signatory directors; travel bans and international arrest warrants can be issued by the Office of the Attorney General once flight risk is demonstrated).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Abuse & Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss shipyard or a parallel trading/holding company without bona fide business activity: no office, employees, independent decision-taking or bank account management in Switzerland; using the Swiss entity solely to re-invoice container-vessel sales, to accumulate participation dividends and to benefit from the participation relief or patent box without substantive R&D; entering into a back-to-back loan structure aimed at converting dividends into deductible interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under Art. 219 DBG (Steuerumgehung): consequent assessment of the tax as if the economic substance were at the place of management; repayment of treaty relief; 35% withholding tax on the disguised dividend plus 5% default interest and penalties; pursuant to the DTA limitation-of-benefits clauses, the foreign parent may lose all treaty protection on the repatriated stream.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors who signed the substance-less agreements are jointly liable for the additional corporate tax, withholding tax and procedural fines; in aggravated abuse the court may set aside the legal entity (veil-piercing) and order restitution of the tax advantage from the shareholder individually; board members may also face disqualification from serving as administrators for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering & Sanctions (Trading with a 'Medium-Risk, Enhanced' profile)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash payments above CHF 100,000 per transaction in the ship supply or commission business without due diligence; concealing the beneficial owner of an escrow or foreign-payment structure; operating trade-based money laundering schemes through over- or under-invoiced container-vessel component purchases; executing maritime sales contracts with sanctioned states or state-owned shipping companies in circumvention of Swiss SECO/State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, OFAC or EU embargoes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: As a merchant in goods (AMLA Art. 2 para. 3 scope), the shipyard is a financial intermediary only when receiving cash ≥ CHF 100,000; violation of due diligence and reporting obligations is sanctioned by imprisonment up to one year or a fine; money laundering under Art. 305bis SCC is punishable by imprisonment up to three years (five for aggravated cases) and total confiscation of assets; breach of Swiss embargoes (Embargo Act) entails imprisonment up to ten years in qualified cases and blacklisting of the company from public procurement and export financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and beneficial owners are prosecuted as perpetrators or accomplices; personal imprisonment up to five years, prohibition on exercising management functions, seizure of personal real estate and bank accounts, issuance of an international wanted notice, and joint and several civil liability to the company for losses caused by the violation (Art. 717 Code of Obligations duty of care).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accounting of above-market interest on shareholder loans, missing TP documentation for related-party engine or steel purchases, non-application of the arm's length principle for the vessel construction margin charged to foreign related buyers (sales/distribution functions), and absence of a written transfer pricing policy when the related-party transaction volume exceeds CHF 1 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of taxable income by the canton with reconstitution of an arm's length profit, additional corporate tax plus interest; hidden profit distribution reclassification triggers 35% withholding tax on the excess interest or royalty paid to the foreign shareholder; the ESTV may impose the procedural fine under Art. 174 DBG (up to CHF 10,000) for non-production of records; for groups >EUR 750 million revenue, penalty for missing GloBE Information Return and top-up tax up to 15% effective rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The finance director and management board are jointly liable for the tax adjustment and the punitive withholding tax payment; in the presence of fraudulent documentation, the matter crosses into tax deception with personal criminal liability (up to two years imprisonment) and, in cross-border cases, the secondment of the case to the Federal Criminal Police for money-laundering assessment of fund flows.
